question: How do the in-season award odds (NBA, NFL, NHL, CFB) compare with traded prices?
answer: The market is far ahead. Winner log loss was 2.34 for the model and 1.22 for Polymarket on the 2025-26 races.
findings: Held 2025-26: 19 race-checkpoints over 10 races. The model was 2.345 and the market 1.218, and the market was better in 7 of 10 (t = 2.44).
Tuning 2024-25: 17 race-checkpoints over 7 races. The model was 2.045 and the market 1.098.
A temperature fit to the market (T 1.5) didn't help on outcomes. The held change was -.07 (t = -.53).
The first CFB backtest (2005-25, 246 checkpoints) had the favourite at .33/.37/.42, against a hit rate of .11/.24/.31, at 25/50/75%.
method: The races are rebuilt as of 25/50/75% of each season, with voter fits that leave one season out (scripts/awards_asof.py). The market is the Polymarket (global) daily price of the eventual winner on the day after the checkpoint, renormalised over the listed candidates. Checkpoints whose prices sum more than 25% off 1 are dropped as illiquid.
data: scripts/data/poly_hist (36 closed events, 2024-26); nflverse, in-repo NBA boxes, sportsdataverse ESPN CFB boxes.
split_check: The market was ahead in both seasons (2024-25 and 2025-26).
